newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares end lower, seen oscillating.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares end lower, seen oscillating.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.63 percent on Monday and traders said little change could be expected while negotiations for a new government continued in the wake of elections two weeks ago.
"Investors are waiting for a new government or any other sparkle that will enliven the market," one broker said.
Prices could tread water for several weeks as it may take over a month to form the government, she noted.

The current ruling Liberal Democrats emerged as the strongest single party with 25 out of 90 parliamentary seats, but face a rightist "Spring" alliance comprising three parties which together received 45 seats -- just one seat short of an absolute majority.

Traders predicted volumes would rise in the second half of December regardless of the political situation as a significant number of small shareholders were likely to sell off stocks to avoid a new 25-percent tax on profit from trade in securities that will be introduced from January.
"That may push prices slightly down just before the end of the year," one trader said.
Until now only corporate shareholders have had to pay tax on profit made in securities.
The 10-share SBI index fell 7.23 points to 1,159.4.
Seven shares rose, nine fell, two were unchanged and seven were untraded.
Turnover eased to 168.1 million tolars from 186.1 million on Friday.
Financial consultancy Finmedia was most actively traded, rising 2.07 percent to 16,740 tolars on volume of 3,712 shares for total turnover of 62.7 million tolars.
Construction copmany GPG was the top decliner, falling 8.88 percent to 7,080 on volume of 500 shares for total turnover of 3.5 million tolars.

Preferred shares of bank Hipotekarna Banka Brezice were the leading gainers, closing 9.91 percent higher at 3,660 on volume of 150 shares for total turnover of 0.5 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana Newsroom 368 61 1263 644
